The hyperstability version of the Erdős–Gallai theorem says, roughly, that a `C_d`-free graph can
be turned — by deleting few edges — into a graph all of whose connected components have a small
vertex cover.  This file establishes the *tightness* of the edge-deletion bound: the balanced
complete bipartite graph `K_{t,t}` shows that one may be forced to delete on the order of `c·d·n`
edges.

The extremal construction `K_{t,t}` is realized here as the complete `2`-equipartite graph
`completeEquipartiteGraph 2 t` on the vertex set `Fin 2 × Fin t` (so `n = 2t`).

## Main pieces (each proved independently, avoiding any circular dependency)

* `Ktt_closed_walk_even` / `Ktt_Cd_free` — **Lemma 1**: `K_{t,t}` contains no cycle of odd length
  (indeed no closed walk of odd length), proved purely from bipartiteness (a `Bool`-coloring).
* `Ktt_card_edges` — **Lemma 2**: `K_{t,t}` has exactly `t²` edges.
* `edge_card_le_of_blockwise_cover` / `edge_card_le_of_componentwise_cover` — **Lemma 3**: the local
  density bound.  If every connected component of a graph `H` has a vertex cover of size `≤ k`, then
  `H` has at most `k·n` edges.  Proved from first principles by an injection of the edges into a
  block-wise product `S_b × V_b`.
* `hyperstability_edge_deletion_tight` — **Main theorem**: combining the three lemmas, any subgraph
  `H ≤ K_{t,t}` whose components each have a vertex cover of size `≤ (1+c)d` requires deleting at
  least `c·d·n` edges, where `n = 2t` and `t = 2(1+2c)d`.

import Mathlib

open SimpleGraph Finset

namespace ErdosGallaiHyperstability

/-- The balanced complete bipartite graph `K_{t,t}`, realized as the complete `2`-equipartite
graph on `Fin 2 × Fin t`.  Its vertex set has `n = 2t` vertices. -/
abbrev Ktt (t : ℕ) : SimpleGraph (Fin 2 × Fin t) := completeEquipartiteGraph 2 t

/-! ### Lemma 1: `K_{t,t}` has no odd (closed) walk -/

/-- A `Bool`-coloring of `K_{t,t}`: colour a vertex by which side it lies on. -/
def KttColoring (t : ℕ) : (Ktt t).Coloring Bool :=
  SimpleGraph.Coloring.mk (fun v => decide (v.1 = 1)) (by
    intro v w h
    rw [Ktt, completeEquipartiteGraph_adj] at h
    simp only [ne_eq, decide_eq_decide]
    intro hc
    exact h (by omega))

/-- **Lemma 1 (core).** Every closed walk in `K_{t,t}` has even length (bipartiteness). -/
theorem Ktt_closed_walk_even (t : ℕ) (u : Fin 2 × Fin t) (p : (Ktt t).Walk u u) :
    Even p.length := by
  rw [(KttColoring t).even_length_iff_congr p]

/-- **Lemma 1.** For odd `d`, `K_{t,t}` contains no cycle of length `d` (indeed no closed walk of
length `d`). -/
theorem Ktt_Cd_free (t d : ℕ) (hodd : Odd d) :
    ¬ ∃ (u : Fin 2 × Fin t) (p : (Ktt t).Walk u u), p.IsCycle ∧ p.length = d := by
  rintro ⟨u, p, _, hlen⟩
  have := Ktt_closed_walk_even t u p
  rw [hlen] at this
  exact (Nat.not_even_iff_odd.2 hodd) this

/-! ### Lemma 2: edge count of `K_{t,t}` -/

/-- **Lemma 2.** `K_{t,t}` has exactly `t²` edges. -/
theorem Ktt_card_edges (t : ℕ) : (Ktt t).edgeFinset.card = t ^ 2 := by
  have h : (Ktt t).edgeFinset.card = (2 : ℕ).choose 2 * t ^ 2 :=
    card_edgeFinset_completeEquipartiteGraph
  simpa using h

/-! ### Lemma 3: local density bound from component-wise vertex covers -/

/-
**Lemma 3 (general form).** If for every "block" `b` (a value of the labelling `part`, whose
level sets refine the components of `H`, i.e. adjacent vertices share a label) there is a vertex
set `S` inside that block, of size `≤ k`, covering all edges of `H` inside the block, then `H` has
at most `k·|V|` edges.

Proof idea (first principles): map each edge to `(c, w)` where `c` is a cover vertex on the edge
and `w` is the other endpoint.  This injects the edges of block `b` into `S_b × V_b`, of size
`≤ k·|V_b|`; summing over blocks (which partition `V`) gives `≤ k·Σ|V_b| = k·|V|`.
-/
theorem edge_card_le_of_blockwise_cover
    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (H : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel H.Adj]
    {β : Type*} (part : V → β)
    (hpart : ∀ ⦃u v⦄, H.Adj u v → part u = part v) (k : ℕ)
    (hcov : ∀ b : β, ∃ S : Finset V, (∀ v ∈ S, part v = b) ∧ S.card ≤ k ∧
              ∀ ⦃u v⦄, H.Adj u v → part u = b → (u ∈ S ∨ v ∈ S)) :
    H.edgeFinset.card ≤ k * Fintype.card V := by
  choose S hS₁ hS₂ hS₃ using hcov;
  -- Define `D` as the union of products of covers and blocks.
  set D : Finset (V × V) := Finset.biUnion (Finset.univ : Finset V) (fun w => (S (part w)).image (fun c => (c, w))) with hD_def;
  -- By definition of $D$, we know that every edge in $H$ is mapped to a unique pair in $D$.
  have h_inj : ∀ e ∈ H.edgeFinset, ∃ p ∈ D, e = Sym2.mk p := by
    intro e he; rcases e with ⟨ u, v ⟩ ; simp_all +decide [ SimpleGraph.adj_comm ] ;
    grind;
  have h_card_D : H.edgeFinset.card ≤ D.card := by
    have h_card_D : H.edgeFinset.card ≤ Finset.card (Finset.image (fun p => Sym2.mk p) D) := by
      exact Finset.card_le_card fun e he => by obtain ⟨ p, hp, rfl ⟩ := h_inj e he; exact Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ hp;
    exact h_card_D.trans ( Finset.card_image_le );
  refine' le_trans h_card_D ( le_trans ( Finset.card_biUnion_le ) _ );
  exact le_trans ( Finset.sum_le_sum fun _ _ => Finset.card_image_le.trans ( hS₂ _ ) ) ( by simp +decide [ mul_comm ] )

/-- A graph `H` has the **component-wise cover property with parameter `k`** if every connected
component admits a vertex cover of size `≤ k` (living inside that component). -/
def ComponentwiseCover {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (H : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ c : H.ConnectedComponent, ∃ S : Finset V,
    (∀ v ∈ S, H.connectedComponentMk v = c) ∧ S.card ≤ k ∧
    (∀ ⦃u v⦄, H.Adj u v → H.connectedComponentMk u = c → (u ∈ S ∨ v ∈ S))

/-- **Lemma 3.** If every connected component of `H` has a vertex cover of size `≤ k`, then `H`
has at most `k·|V|` edges. -/
theorem edge_card_le_of_componentwise_cover
    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (H : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel H.Adj] (k : ℕ)
    (hcov : ComponentwiseCover H k) :
    H.edgeFinset.card ≤ k * Fintype.card V := by
  apply edge_card_le_of_blockwise_cover H H.connectedComponentMk _ k hcov
  intro u v h
  exact ConnectedComponent.sound h.reachable

/-! ### Arithmetic core -/

/-- The standalone arithmetic inequality behind the tightness bound:
`t² ≥ (1+2c)·d·(2t)` whenever `t ≥ 2(1+2c)d`. -/
theorem tightness_arith (c d t : ℕ) (ht : 2 * (1 + 2 * c) * d ≤ t) :
    (1 + 2 * c) * d * (2 * t) ≤ t ^ 2 := by
  nlinarith [ht, Nat.zero_le t]

/-! ### Main theorem -/

/-- **Tightness of the edge-deletion bound in the hyperstability Erdős–Gallai theorem.**

For every positive stability parameter `c` and every odd `d ≥ 3`, there is a `C_d`-free graph `G`
(the balanced complete bipartite graph `K_{t,t}` with `t = 2(1+2c)d`, on `n = 2t` vertices) such
that any subgraph `H ≤ G` all of whose connected components have a vertex cover of size `≤ (1+c)d`
can be obtained from `G` only by deleting at least `c·d·n` edges.

The hypotheses `hc : 1 ≤ c` and `hd3 : 3 ≤ d` are kept because they are part of the stated setting
(`c > 0`, `d ≥ 3`); the proof does not actually need them (the bound is vacuous/monotone in these
corner cases), only `hodd : Odd d` is used, to guarantee `C_d`-freeness. -/
theorem hyperstability_edge_deletion_tight
    (c d : ℕ) (hc : 1 ≤ c) (hd3 : 3 ≤ d) (hodd : Odd d) :
    ∃ (t : ℕ) (n : ℕ),
      n = Fintype.card (Fin 2 × Fin t) ∧
      n = 2 * t ∧
      -- `G = K_{t,t}` is `C_d`-free
      (¬ ∃ (u : Fin 2 × Fin t) (p : (Ktt t).Walk u u), p.IsCycle ∧ p.length = d) ∧
      -- `G` has `t²` edges
      (Ktt t).edgeFinset.card = t ^ 2 ∧
      -- every admissible `H` requires deleting at least `c·d·n` edges
      (∀ (H : SimpleGraph (Fin 2 × Fin t)) [DecidableRel H.Adj], H ≤ Ktt t →
         ComponentwiseCover H ((1 + c) * d) →
         c * d * n ≤ ((Ktt t).edgeFinset \ H.edgeFinset).card) := by
  refine ⟨2 * (1 + 2 * c) * d, 2 * (2 * (1 + 2 * c) * d), ?_, ?_,
    Ktt_Cd_free _ d hodd, Ktt_card_edges _, ?_⟩
  · simp [mul_comm]
  · rfl
  · intro H hinst hHle hcov
    have hcard : Fintype.card (Fin 2 × Fin (2 * (1 + 2 * c) * d))
        = 2 * (2 * (1 + 2 * c) * d) := by simp [Fintype.card_prod]
    have hHedges : H.edgeFinset.card ≤ (1 + c) * d * (2 * (2 * (1 + 2 * c) * d)) := by
      have h := edge_card_le_of_componentwise_cover H ((1 + c) * d) hcov
      rwa [hcard] at h
    have hsub : H.edgeFinset ⊆ (Ktt (2 * (1 + 2 * c) * d)).edgeFinset :=
      edgeFinset_mono hHle
    have hG : (Ktt (2 * (1 + 2 * c) * d)).edgeFinset.card = (2 * (1 + 2 * c) * d) ^ 2 :=
      Ktt_card_edges _
    have harith : (1 + 2 * c) * d * (2 * (2 * (1 + 2 * c) * d))
        ≤ (2 * (1 + 2 * c) * d) ^ 2 :=
      tightness_arith c d (2 * (1 + 2 * c) * d) (le_refl _)
    have key : c * d * (2 * (2 * (1 + 2 * c) * d)) + H.edgeFinset.card
        ≤ (2 * (1 + 2 * c) * d) ^ 2 := by nlinarith [hHedges, harith]
    have hsdiff := card_sdiff_of_subset hsub
    rw [hG] at hsdiff
    omega

# Future Directions

Derived from this cycle's finding: the balanced complete bipartite graph
`K_{t,t}` on `n = 2t` vertices is `C_d`-free for odd `d`, packs `n²/4` edges, and
requires at least `cd·n` edge deletions to reach a graph whose components each
admit a vertex cover of size `(1+c)d` — with equality at the threshold
`t = 2(1+2c)d`. This certifies that the `cd·n` edge-deletion bound in the
hyperstable Erdős–Gallai regime is order-optimal.

## 1. A tight `C_d`-free witness for *even* cycle lengths

The balanced bipartite construction only avoids *odd* cycles, so it certifies
tightness for odd `d`. For even `d`, one needs a dense host graph whose shortest
even cycle exceeds `d` while retaining a linear-in-`n` vertex-cover deficit.
**Conjecture:** for every even `d` there is a graph on `n` vertices, free of
cycles of length exactly `d`, from which at least `cd·n` edge deletions are needed
to reach the bounded-component-cover regime. **The key insight is** that
incidence graphs of generalized polygons and Wenger-type algebraic graphs have
prescribed girth yet super-linear edge density, decoupling "no short even cycle"
from sparsity. **Why now?** The odd case pins down the exact target constant, so
the even case becomes a concrete, quantitative girth-versus-density question with
a known numerical goalpost rather than an open-ended search.

## 2. The exact optimal constant in front of `d·n`

Our witness meets the bound `cd·n` with equality only at the boundary
`t = 2(1+2c)d`; above it the deleted-edge surplus grows quadratically.
**Conjecture:** the true minimax deletion cost, minimized over all `C_d`-free
hosts on `n` vertices and maximized over the required cover budget, equals
`(1/2)·cd·n + o(dn)`, i.e. the sharp constant is `1/2`, achieved by an
*unbalanced* bipartite host `K_{a,b}` with `a/b → ` a specific function of `c`.
**The key insight is** that skewing the two sides trades raw edge count against
the size of the cheapest vertex cover, and the optimal skew is where the marginal
edge gain equals the marginal cover cost. **Why now?** The balanced case fixes
the order of magnitude and an explicit achievable value, turning "what is the
constant?" into a one-parameter optimization with a verified upper anchor.

## 3. Stability: are near-extremal hosts essentially complete bipartite?

The construction is extremal; the natural next question is uniqueness.
**Conjecture:** any `C_d`-free graph on `n` vertices that requires within a
`(1-ε)` factor of the maximal edge-deletion budget is, after deleting `o(n²)`
edges, a balanced complete bipartite graph (for odd `d`). **The key insight is**
that the deletion lower bound is driven entirely by edge density against a
vertex-cover ceiling, and only bipartite-like graphs simultaneously maximize
density and forbid the relevant cycle — any deviation creates either a forbidden
cycle or a cheap cover. **Why now?** Hyperstability results have recently been
established for cycle counts; porting that machinery to the *edge-deletion metric*
is the missing structural counterpart to the extremal bound proved here.

## 4. From edge deletions to a vertex-deletion / mixed budget

Instead of deleting edges, one may delete vertices (or pay a mixed cost) to reach
small component covers. **Conjecture:** to reduce `K_{t,t}` to components of
vertex cover `≤ (1+c)d` one must delete at least `t − (1+c)d ≈ n/2` vertices, and
more generally the edge-cost and vertex-cost are related by
`edge-cost ≈ (n/2)·vertex-cost` for the extremal host. **The key insight is** that
in a complete bipartite graph a single vertex deletion removes an entire linear
slab of edges, so the two modification metrics are linked by the (linear) degree,
not independent. **Why now?** Graph-modification problems are increasingly studied
under simultaneous budgets; the clean extremal example here gives an exact anchor
for calibrating the exchange rate between the two resources.

## 5. Weighted and multipartite generalizations of the density slab bound

The engine behind the lower bound is: *if every connected component has a vertex
cover of size `≤ k`, the graph has at most `k·n` edges.* **Conjecture:** the
weighted analogue holds — for edge weights in `[0,1]`, the total weight is at most
`k·n`, and more sharply, for `r`-partite-cover budgets the bound improves to
`k·n·(1 − 1/r)`. **The key insight is** that the per-component charging argument
is agnostic to multiplicities and localizes to each component's degree profile,
so it should tensor with weights and with a partite refinement of the cover.
**Why now?** The unweighted slab bound is now isolated as a standalone lemma;
generalizing it is the natural way to extend tightness statements to weighted
Turán-type and to hypergraph Erdős–Gallai settings where cover budgets recur.
